title: Stripr on PayBox: agents that know when to say no

lines.text: AI agents can move money now. Swap, send, sign. One wrong call, and it is gone.
PayBox fixes half of that. Your agent gets a wallet, never the keys. And you approve every move.
Refused. Rule S G zero two, size cap. Thirty four thousand dollars is over the five thousand dollar cap. No transaction was built.
The other half? An agent that knows when to say no.

Stripr is live on Solana mainnet, with fifteen tokenized stocks. Apple, Nvidia, Tesla, and more. Their dividends arrive by growing the token itself. Coca-Cola's has grown by two point two six percent.
But the share and its dividends come as one. You cannot keep one and sell the other.
Stripr splits a tokenized stock in two. A Principal Token, the share. And a Yield Token, its dividends. Keep one. Trade the other.
Here is the real session. Claude, connected to PayBox, finds the Stripr plugin. It reads the wallet, then previews a split. What you get, the yield, and the fees, before anything moves.
Ask it to split a hundred, and it stops. The wallet holds too little, and the size cap would refuse it anyway. Nothing is built.
The first approval window timed out before I signed. Claude would not create a duplicate. So I asked for a fresh one.
This time it goes through. An unsigned transaction. You approve. PayBox signs. The plugin never touches a key.
Then a redeem, back to the stock. Same approval. Same flow.
Both settle on Solana mainnet. Claude reads back the new position, with an Explorer link.
Before every trade, four plain rules run. Stale price. Size cap. Depeg. Unknown market. If one trips, the agent refuses and names the rule. No model in the path.
Ask for DOGE, and it declines. Stripr does not list it.
What makes it different? It is deterministic. Same inputs, same verdict. It is non-custodial. PayBox signs, never the plugin. And it runs on mainnet today.
And it is live. A real split and a real redeem, on Solana mainnet. Fifteen markets. Fees exactly as quoted.
Stripr on PayBox. Agents that know when to say no.
